THE SECOND USER DESCRIBES HIS OWN WORKING PATH, AND IT IS INDEPENDENT FIELD CONFIRMATION OF AN ACCEPTED REQUIREMENT. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-11. His input is ADVISORY per rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word and nothing here moves any status.

HIS PATH, VERBATIM: "I know I want to do the following things (...). Record those at a high level. Now let's order them. And finally, let's tackle them one at a time and brainstorm." Plus: "I've used brainstorm. I said I want to brainstorm on how to do this and it launched the skill. I have basically been using /where-am-i but I'll be more explicit about it."

⭐⭐ CONFIRMS `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) FROM THE FIELD RATHER THAN FROM SELF-MEASUREMENT. That requirement's own statement, measured on this repo 2026-07-31, says: "exactly two skills were loaded all session, and both only because THE USER TYPED A SLASH COMMAND" — and names capture-intent, report-friction and four others as never loaded. Its rule is that skill use must be "triggered by the situation, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER."

Map his four-step path onto the served kit and the pattern is exact:
  step 1  "record those at a high level"        -> capture-intent      NOT NAMED BY HIM
  step 2  "now let's order them"                 -> plan-increments     NOT NAMED BY HIM
  step 3  "tackle them one at a time"            -> (his own framing)
  step 4  "and brainstorm"                       -> brainstorm          NAMED, and he typed it
  entry   "basically been using /where-am-i"     -> where-am-i          NAMED, and he types it

HE NAMES EXACTLY THE TWO HE TYPES. The two that would fire on a situation he is already in are the two he does not mention — and both exist, are served, and do precisely his steps 1 and 2. He is not failing to read; the trigger mechanism does not reach him, which is what the requirement says.

⭐ AND THE SHARPEST INSTANCE IS IN HIS SECOND TOPIC. He asked for a feedback skill to be built — "put the skill in your skills" — and `report-friction` IS ALREADY SHIPPED IN THE KIT, one of eighteen under getting-started/skills/. A user asked for a capability he already has. That is the same requirement firing a third time in one message, and it is the most expensive form of it: not a skill unused, but a skill REQUESTED WHILE INSTALLED.

HIS SECOND TOPIC, VERBATIM, and the genuinely new part: "You should put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph or something. And put the skill in your skills. That way you get what you want." The skill half is already satisfied. The CONSENT half is not — see dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED HERE: one user, relayed rather than observed directly, and his path is a description of intent rather than a transcript. It confirms the shape the accepted requirement already states; it is not new evidence about how often skills are missed.
